rubrics.evidence: Final selection rules: “Choose independent venture building as the central learning mechanism regardless of which educational format you add.” Phases 2–4 require customer interviews, willingness-to-pay tests, an MVP and paid pilots.
rubrics.reason: Practical venture building determines the roadmap and its deliverables. A second general business degree is explicitly deprioritized and retained only for specific ecosystem or career-transition benefits.

rubrics.evidence: The baseline is a “12-month validation track at 6–8 hours per week.” Phase 4 requires cohort work to coexist with employment, and the overload rules state: “A demanding cohort program should replace, not supplement, most self-study.”
rubrics.reason: Work and family constraints materially govern scheduling, course load and program selection. Intensive accelerators and full-time degrees are conditional options requiring an explicit career and family decision.

rubrics.evidence: Phase 1 includes weekly interviews and applied work; Phase 2 conducts customer discovery in Months 2–4; Phase 3 requires the “cheapest credible test,” such as a concierge service, deposit or small paid pilot. The Month 6 gate directs weak ideas to be pivoted or archived.
rubrics.reason: Real customer contact starts during the compact foundation stage, followed by low-cost behavioral and payment tests. Explicit kill criteria and progression gates make validation consequential rather than postponing it until extensive study is complete.

rubrics.evidence: Phase 3 says to use the Business Model Canvas “as a versioned hypothesis system” and “Update it only when evidence changes.” Required metrics include conversion to payment, repeat use, acquisition cost and refusal reasons; later phases require a 13-week cash forecast and financing scenarios.
rubrics.reason: Concrete frameworks and market evidence directly inform product, pricing, financing and continuation decisions. Although in-depth case study is less developed, the learning approach is clearly application-driven rather than predominantly theoretical.

rubrics.evidence: The report rejects expensive programs that duplicate MBA content, sets lean and structured budget routes, and states: “If evidence is weak, pivot once or archive the idea. Do not respond by buying a more expensive course.” Degree evaluation includes tuition, lost compensation and family disruption.
rubrics.reason: Cost, workload, opportunity cost and practical incremental value materially shape the recommended sequence. Prestige-oriented options remain conditional and must justify their cost through relevant networks, capabilities or venture outcomes.
